summary: This benchmark conducts a rigorous differential analysis of seven widely used Git configuration parser libraries across Python, Node.js, Go, and Rust against canonical git config output. Using a 76-file synthetic suite and a 39-repository dotfiles corpus, the authors demonstrate systematic discrepancies in quote stripping, line continuation, and bare boolean handling, particularly in INI-derived parsers.
strengths: Rigorous differential testing methodology treating git config --list -z as the ground-truth oracle.
Comprehensive test case coverage (76 synthetic edge cases categorized into structure, names, subsections, values, and practical files).
Empirical grounding via 39 pinned real-world dotfiles repositories demonstrating real-world prevalence of syntax misinterpretations.
Careful taxonomy of deviations (A, T, W, R, L) distinguishing harmless canonicalizations from functional or potential injection flaws.
weaknesses: Isomorphic-git is tested by inspecting internal/undocumented fields (parsedConfig) rather than purely public consumer APIs.
The evaluation is restricted to read operations with default options and ignores include/includeIf directives and configuration writers.
Only a single reference Git version (2.47.3) is used, leaving historical parser behavior changes untested.
suggestions: Extend the test harness to evaluate include and includeIf conditional resolution across libraries supporting it.
Test multi-version Git baselines to document when specific edge-case behaviors (like bare keys or end-of-file backslashes) stabilized.
Submit upstream bug reports or conformance pull requests to the affected libraries (especially parse-git-config and go-git).

claims.text: CVE-2023-29007 was a git bug in which a value longer than 1024 bytes, written back during a section rename, was split so that a [ in the remainder started a new section; a malicious .gitmodules could thereby set core.pager or core.sshCommand.
The git-config documentation defines a variable with no = that means boolean true, which is different from an empty value that means false.

The git-config documentation defines case-insensitive section and variable names but case-sensitive subsection names; double-quoted subsections with their own escapes; values in which double quotes are removed and may appear anywhere, # and ; start a comment only outside quotes, and the escapes \n, \t, \b, \" and \\ are recognised while any other escape is an error.
